result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

declarations.name: Convex.taylor_approx_two_segment
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem Convex.taylor_approx_two_segment {v w : E} (hv : x + v ∈ interior s)
    (hw : x + v + w ∈ interior s) :
    (fun h : ℝ => f (x + h • v + h • w)
        - f (x + h • v) - h • f' x w - h ^ 2 • f'' v w - (h ^ 2 / 2) • f'' w w) =o[𝓝[>] 0]
      fun h => h ^ 2
declarations.doc:
Assume that `f` is differentiable inside a convex set `s`, and that its derivative `f'` is
differentiable at a point `x`. Then, given two vectors `v` and `w` pointing inside `s`, one can
Taylor-expand to order two the function `f` on the segment `[x + h v, x + h (v + w)]`, giving a
bilinear estimate for `f (x + hv + hw) - f (x + hv)` in terms of `f' w` and of `f'' ⬝ w`, up to
`o(h^2)`.

This is a technical statement used to show that the second derivative is symmetric.

declarations.name: Lean.Meta.mkRichHCongr
declarations.source_snippet:
partial def mkRichHCongr (fType : Expr) (info : FunInfo)
    (fixedFun : Bool := false) (fixedParams : Array Bool := #[])
    (forceHEq : Bool := false) :
    MetaM CongrTheorem := do
  trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "ftype: {fType}"
  trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "deps: {info.paramInfo.map (fun p => p.backDeps)}"
  trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "fixedFun={fixedFun}, fixedParams={fixedParams}"
  doubleTelescope fType info.getArity fixedParams fun xs ys fixedParams => do
    trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "xs = {xs}"
    trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "ys = {ys}"
    trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "computed fixedParams={fixedParams}"
    let lctx := (← getLCtx)                                                               
    withLocalDeclD `f fType fun ef => withLocalDeclD `f' fType fun pef' => do
    let ef' := if fixedFun then ef else pef'
    withLocalDeclD `e (← mkEq ef ef') fun ee => do
    withNewEqs xs ys fixedParams fun kinds eqs => do
      let fParams := if fixedFun then #[ef] else #[ef, ef', ee]

declarations.name: Lean.Meta.mkRichHCongr
declarations.source_snippet:
partial def mkRichHCongr (fType : Expr) (info : FunInfo)
    (fixedFun : Bool := false) (fixedParams : Array Bool := #[])
    (forceHEq : Bool := false) :
    MetaM CongrTheorem := do
  trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "ftype: {fType}"
  trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "deps: {info.paramInfo.map (fun p => p.backDeps)}"
  trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "fixedFun={fixedFun}, fixedParams={fixedParams}"
  doubleTelescope fType info.getArity fixedParams fun xs ys fixedParams => do
    trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "xs = {xs}"
    trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "ys = {ys}"
    trace[Meta.CongrTheorems] "computed fixedParams={fixedParams}"
    let lctx := (← getLCtx)                                                               
    withLocalDeclD `f fType fun ef => withLocalDeclD `f' fType fun pef' => do
    let ef' := if fixedFun then ef else pef'
    withLocalDeclD `e (← mkEq ef ef') fun ee => do
    withNewEqs xs ys fixedParams fun kinds eqs => do
      let fParams := if fixedFun then #[ef] else #[ef, ef', ee]

declarations.name: Monotone.stieltjesFunction
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.Monotone.stieltjesFunction {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Monotone f) :
    StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := rightLim f
  mono' _ _ hxy := hf.rightLim hxy
  right_continuous' := by
    intro x s hs
    obtain ⟨l, u, hlu, lus⟩ : ∃ l u : ℝ, rightLim f x ∈ Ioo l u ∧ Ioo l u ⊆ s :=
      mem_nhds_iff_exists_Ioo_subset.1 hs
    obtain ⟨y, xy, h'y⟩ : ∃ (y : ℝ), x < y ∧ Ioc x y ⊆ f ⁻¹' Ioo l u :=
      mem_nhdsWithin_Ioi_iff_exists_Ioc_subset.1 (hf.tendsto_rightLim x (Ioo_mem_nhds hlu.1 hlu.2))
    change ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≥] x, rightLim f y ∈ s
    filter_upwards [Ico_mem_nhdsWithin_Ici ⟨le_refl x, xy⟩] with z hz
    apply lus
    refine ⟨hlu.1.trans_le (hf.rightLim hz.1), ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨a, za, ay⟩ : ∃ a : ℝ, z < a ∧ a < y := exists_between hz.2
    calc
      rightLim f z ≤ f a := hf.rightLim_le za
      _ < u := (h'y ⟨hz.1.trans_lt za, ay.le⟩).2
declarations.doc:
If a function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is monotone, then the function mapping `x` to the right limit of `f`
at `x` is a Stieltjes function, i.e., it is monotone and right-continuous.

  right_has_deriv : HasStrictFDerivAt rightFun rightDeriv pt

declarations.name: Monotone.stieltjesFunction
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.Monotone.stieltjesFunction {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Monotone f) :
    StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := rightLim f
  mono' _ _ hxy := hf.rightLim hxy
  right_continuous' := by
    intro x s hs
    obtain ⟨l, u, hlu, lus⟩ : ∃ l u : ℝ, rightLim f x ∈ Ioo l u ∧ Ioo l u ⊆ s :=
      mem_nhds_iff_exists_Ioo_subset.1 hs
    obtain ⟨y, xy, h'y⟩ : ∃ (y : ℝ), x < y ∧ Ioc x y ⊆ f ⁻¹' Ioo l u :=
      mem_nhdsWithin_Ioi_iff_exists_Ioc_subset.1 (hf.tendsto_rightLim x (Ioo_mem_nhds hlu.1 hlu.2))
    change ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≥] x, rightLim f y ∈ s
    filter_upwards [Ico_mem_nhdsWithin_Ici ⟨le_refl x, xy⟩] with z hz
    apply lus
    refine ⟨hlu.1.trans_le (hf.rightLim hz.1), ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨a, za, ay⟩ : ∃ a : ℝ, z < a ∧ a < y := exists_between hz.2
    calc
      rightLim f z ≤ f a := hf.rightLim_le za
      _ < u := (h'y ⟨hz.1.trans_lt za, ay.le⟩).2
declarations.doc:
If a function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is monotone, then the function mapping `x` to the right limit of `f`
at `x` is a Stieltjes function, i.e., it is monotone and right-continuous.

declarations.name: IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure
declarations.source_snippet:
class IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure {α : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace α] [MeasurableSpace α]
  (μ : Measure α) : Prop where
  exists_measure_closedBall_le_mul'' :
    ∃ C : ℝ≥0, ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] 0, ∀ x, μ (closedBall x (2 * ε)) ≤ C * μ (closedBall x ε)
declarations.doc:
A measure `μ` is said to be a uniformly locally doubling measure if there exists a constant `C`
such that for all sufficiently small radii `ε`, and for any centre, the measure of a ball of radius
`2 * ε` is bounded by `C` times the measure of the concentric ball of radius `ε`.

Note: it is important that this definition makes a demand only for sufficiently small `ε`. For
example we want hyperbolic space to carry the instance `IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure volume` but
volumes grow exponentially in hyperbolic space. To be really explicit, consider the hyperbolic plane
of curvature -1, the area of a disc of radius `ε` is `A(ε) = 2π(cosh(ε) - 1)` so
`A(2ε)/A(ε) ~ exp(ε)`.

declarations.name: Monotone.stieltjesFunction
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.Monotone.stieltjesFunction {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Monotone f) :
    StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := rightLim f
  mono' _ _ hxy := hf.rightLim hxy
  right_continuous' := by
    intro x s hs
    obtain ⟨l, u, hlu, lus⟩ : ∃ l u : ℝ, rightLim f x ∈ Ioo l u ∧ Ioo l u ⊆ s :=
      mem_nhds_iff_exists_Ioo_subset.1 hs
    obtain ⟨y, xy, h'y⟩ : ∃ (y : ℝ), x < y ∧ Ioc x y ⊆ f ⁻¹' Ioo l u :=
      mem_nhdsWithin_Ioi_iff_exists_Ioc_subset.1 (hf.tendsto_rightLim x (Ioo_mem_nhds hlu.1 hlu.2))
    change ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≥] x, rightLim f y ∈ s
    filter_upwards [Ico_mem_nhdsWithin_Ici ⟨le_refl x, xy⟩] with z hz
    apply lus
    refine ⟨hlu.1.trans_le (hf.rightLim hz.1), ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨a, za, ay⟩ : ∃ a : ℝ, z < a ∧ a < y := exists_between hz.2
    calc
      rightLim f z ≤ f a := hf.rightLim_le za
      _ < u := (h'y ⟨hz.1.trans_lt za, ay.le⟩).2
declarations.doc:
If a function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is monotone, then the function mapping `x` to the right limit of `f`
at `x` is a Stieltjes function, i.e., it is monotone and right-continuous.

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

declarations.name: Monotone.stieltjesFunction
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.Monotone.stieltjesFunction {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Monotone f) :
    StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := rightLim f
  mono' _ _ hxy := hf.rightLim hxy
  right_continuous' := by
    intro x s hs
    obtain ⟨l, u, hlu, lus⟩ : ∃ l u : ℝ, rightLim f x ∈ Ioo l u ∧ Ioo l u ⊆ s :=
      mem_nhds_iff_exists_Ioo_subset.1 hs
    obtain ⟨y, xy, h'y⟩ : ∃ (y : ℝ), x < y ∧ Ioc x y ⊆ f ⁻¹' Ioo l u :=
      mem_nhdsWithin_Ioi_iff_exists_Ioc_subset.1 (hf.tendsto_rightLim x (Ioo_mem_nhds hlu.1 hlu.2))
    change ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≥] x, rightLim f y ∈ s
    filter_upwards [Ico_mem_nhdsWithin_Ici ⟨le_refl x, xy⟩] with z hz
    apply lus
    refine ⟨hlu.1.trans_le (hf.rightLim hz.1), ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨a, za, ay⟩ : ∃ a : ℝ, z < a ∧ a < y := exists_between hz.2
    calc
      rightLim f z ≤ f a := hf.rightLim_le za
      _ < u := (h'y ⟨hz.1.trans_lt za, ay.le⟩).2
declarations.doc:
If a function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is monotone, then the function mapping `x` to the right limit of `f`
at `x` is a Stieltjes function, i.e., it is monotone and right-continuous.

declarations.name: ConvexOn.curvatureMeasure
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable
irreducible_def curvatureMeasure (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Measure ℝ :=
  if hf : ConvexOn ℝ univ f then hf.rightDerivStieltjes.measure else 0
declarations.doc:
The curvature measure induced by a convex function. It is defined as the only measure that has
the right derivative of the function as a CDF.
For nonconvex functions it is defined as the zero measure.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_integrable
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_integrable
    (hu : ∀ x, HasDerivAt u (u' x) x) (hv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt v (v' x) x)
    (huv' : Integrable (u * v')) (hu'v : Integrable (u' * v)) (huv : Integrable (u * v)) :
    ∫ (x : ℝ), u x * v' x = - ∫ (x : ℝ), u' x * v x
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts on (-∞, ∞).**
Version assuming that the total function is integrable

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul [CompleteSpace A]
    (hu : ∀ x, HasDerivAt u (u' x) x) (hv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt v (v' x) x)
    (huv' : Integrable (u * v')) (hu'v : Integrable (u' * v))
    (h_bot : Tendsto (u * v) atBot (𝓝 a')) (h_top : Tendsto (u * v) atTop (𝓝 b')) :
    ∫ (x : ℝ), u x * v' x = b' - a' - ∫ (x : ℝ), u' x * v x
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts on (-∞, ∞).**
For finite intervals, see: `intervalIntegral.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_hasDerivWithinAt
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_hasDerivWithinAt {u v u' v' : ℝ → A}
    (hu : ∀ x ∈ [[a, b]], HasDerivWithinAt u (u' x) [[a, b]] x)
    (hv : ∀ x ∈ [[a, b]], HasDerivWithinAt v (v' x) [[a, b]] x)
    (hu' : IntervalIntegrable u' volume a b)
    (hv' : IntervalIntegrable v' volume a b) :
    ∫ x in a..b, u x * v' x = u b * v b - u a * v a - ∫ x in a..b, u' x * v x
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts**. Special case of
`intervalIntegrable.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_hasDeriv_right`
where the functions have a one-sided derivative at the endpoints.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_hasDeriv_right
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_hasDeriv_right {u v u' v' : ℝ → A}
    (hu : ContinuousOn u [[a, b]])
    (hv : ContinuousOn v [[a, b]])
    (huu' : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivWithinAt u (u' x) (Ioi x) x)
    (hvv' : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivWithinAt v (v' x) (Ioi x) x)
    (hu' : IntervalIntegrable u' volume a b)
    (hv' : IntervalIntegrable v' volume a b) :
    ∫ x in a..b, u x * v' x = u b * v b - u a * v a - ∫ x in a..b, u' x * v x
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts**. For improper integrals, see
`MeasureTheory.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`,
`MeasureTheory.integral_Ioi_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`,
and `MeasureTheory.integral_Iic_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul {u v u' v' : ℝ → A}
    (hu : ∀ x ∈ [[a, b]], HasDerivAt u (u' x) x)
    (hv : ∀ x ∈ [[a, b]], HasDerivAt v (v' x) x)
    (hu' : IntervalIntegrable u' volume a b)
    (hv' : IntervalIntegrable v' volume a b) :
    ∫ x in a..b, u x * v' x = u b * v b - u a * v a - ∫ x in a..b, u' x * v x

**Integration by parts**. Special case of

and `MeasureTheory.integral_Iic_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.integral_bilinear_hasDerivAt_right_eq_sub
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_bilinear_hasDerivAt_right_eq_sub [CompleteSpace G]
    (hu : ∀ x, HasDerivAt u (u' x) x) (hv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt v (v' x) x)
    (huv' : Integrable (fun x ↦ L (u x) (v' x))) (hu'v : Integrable (fun x ↦ L (u' x) (v x)))
    (h_bot : Tendsto (fun x ↦ L (u x) (v x)) atBot (𝓝 m))
    (h_top : Tendsto (fun x ↦ L (u x) (v x)) atTop (𝓝 n)) :
    ∫ (x : ℝ), L (u x) (v' x) = n - m - ∫ (x : ℝ), L (u' x) (v x)
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts on (-∞, ∞).**
With respect to a general bilinear form. For the specific case of multiplication, see
`integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt` for a version with sets of the form

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

protected def add (f g : StieltjesFunction) : StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := fun x => f x + g x
  mono' := f.mono.add g.mono
  right_continuous' := fun x => (f.right_continuous x).add (g.right_continuous x)

declarations.source_snippet:
lemma integral_stieltjes_meas_by_parts (f g : StieltjesFunction) (a b : ℝ)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) :
    ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂g.measure = (f b) * (g b) - (f a) * (g a) - ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂f.measure
declarations.type:
∀ (f g : StieltjesFunction) (a b : Real),
  ContinuousOn.{0, 0} (↑f) (Set.Icc.{0} a b) →
    Eq.{1} (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, ↑f x ∂StieltjesFunction.measure g)
      (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f b) (↑g b)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f a) (↑g a)))
        (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, ↑g x ∂StieltjesFunction.measure f))
declarations.conclusion:
Eq.{1} (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, ↑f x ∂StieltjesFunction.measure g)
  (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f b) (↑g b)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f a) (↑g a)))
    (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, ↑g x ∂StieltjesFunction.measure f))

      = 2⁻¹ * (∫ x, |β * ((∂μ/∂ν) x).toReal - γ| ∂ν + γ * (ν univ).toReal - β * (μ univ).toReal
        + β * ((μ.singularPart ν) univ).toReal)

  has a right derivative at `f' x` for all `x` in `[a, b)`, and `f'` is integrable on `[a, b]` then
  `∫ y in a..b, f' y` equals `f b - f a`.

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt` for a version with sets of the form
`{ω | f(ω) > t}` instead.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le` for a version with sets of the form `{ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`
instead.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul_of_measurable
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul_of_measurable (μ : Measure α)
    (f_nn : 0 ≤ f) (f_mble : Measurable f)
    (g_intble : ∀ t > 0, IntervalIntegrable g volume 0 t) (g_mble : Measurable g)
    (g_nn : ∀ t > 0, 0 ≤ g t) :
    ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal (∫ t in (0)..f ω, g t) ∂μ =
      ∫⁻ t in Ioi 0, μ {a : α | t ≤ f a} * ENNReal.ofReal (g t)
declarations.doc:
An auxiliary version of the layer cake formula (Cavalieri's principle, tail probability
formula), with a measurability assumption that would also essentially follow from the
integrability assumptions.
Compared to `lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul_of_measurable_of_sigmaFinite`, we remove
the sigma-finite assumption.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul` and
`MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul` for the main formulations of the layer
cake formula.

declarations.doc:
The interval integral `∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ` is defined
as `∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Ioc b a, f x ∂μ`. If `a ≤ b`, then it equals
`∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂μ`, otherwise it equals `-∫ x in Ioc b a, f x ∂μ`.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt
    (f_intble : Integrable f μ) (f_nn : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f) :
    ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ = ∫ t in Set.Ioi 0, ENNReal.toReal (μ {a : α | t < f a})
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For an integrable a.e.-nonnegative real-valued function `f`, the Bochner integral of `f` can be
written (roughly speaking) as: `∫ f ∂μ = ∫ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt` for a version with Lebesgue integral `∫⁻`
instead.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le` for a version with sets of the form `{ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`
instead.

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt
    (f_intble : Integrable f μ) (f_nn : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f) :
    ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ = ∫ t in Set.Ioi 0, ENNReal.toReal (μ {a : α | t < f a})
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For an integrable a.e.-nonnegative real-valued function `f`, the Bochner integral of `f` can be
written (roughly speaking) as: `∫ f ∂μ = ∫ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt` for a version with Lebesgue integral `∫⁻`
instead.

declarations.name: ConvexOn.convex_taylor
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem convex_taylor (hf : ConvexOn ℝ univ f) (hf_cont : Continuous f) {a b : ℝ} :
    f b - f a - (rightDeriv f a) * (b - a)  = ∫ x in a..b, b - x ∂(curvatureMeasure f)
declarations.doc:
A Taylor formula for convex functions in terms of the right derivative
and the curvature measure.
declarations.type:
∀ {f : Real → Real},
  ConvexOn.{0, 0, 0} Real Set.univ.{0} f →
    Continuous.{0, 0} f →
      ∀ {a b : Real},
        Eq.{1}
          (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (f b) (f a))
            (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f a) (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} b a)))
          (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} b x ∂ConvexOn.curvatureMeasure f)
declarations.conclusion:
Eq.{1}
  (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (f b) (f a))
    (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f a) (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} b a)))
  (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} b x ∂ConvexOn.curvatureMeasure f)

    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) :
    ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂g.measure = (f b) * (g b) - (f a) * (g a) - ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂f.measure

      (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f b) (↑g b)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f a) (↑g a)))
        (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, ↑g x ∂StieltjesFunction.measure f))

  (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f b) (↑g b)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f a) (↑g a)))

declarations.name: ConvexOn.rightDerivStieltjes

noncomputable
def rightDerivStieltjes {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ConvexOn ℝ univ f) :
    StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := rightDeriv f
  mono' _ _ := fun h ↦ hf.rightDeriv_mono h
  right_continuous' _ := hf.rightDeriv_right_continuous _

declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.IsCondKernelCDF
declarations.source_snippet:
structure IsCondKernelCDF (f : α × β → StieltjesFunction) (κ : Kernel α (β × ℝ)) (ν : Kernel α β) :
    Prop where
  measurable (x : ℝ) : Measurable fun p ↦ f p x
  integrable (a : α) (x : ℝ) : Integrable (fun b ↦ f (a, b) x) (ν a)
  tendsto_atTop_one (p : α × β) : Tendsto (f p) atTop (𝓝 1)
  tendsto_atBot_zero (p : α × β) : Tendsto (f p) atBot (𝓝 0)
  setIntegral (a : α) {s : Set β} (_hs : MeasurableSet s) (x : ℝ) :
    ∫ b in s, f (a, b) x ∂(ν a) = (κ a (s ×ˢ Iic x)).toReal
declarations.doc:
A function `f : α × β → StieltjesFunction` is called a conditional kernel CDF of `κ` with
respect to `ν` if it is measurable, tends to 0 at -∞ and to 1 at +∞ for all `p : α × β`,
`fun b ↦ f (a, b) x` is `(ν a)`-integrable for all `a : α` and `x : ℝ` and for all
measurable sets `s : Set β`, `∫ b in s, f (a, b) x ∂(ν a) = (κ a (s ×ˢ Iic x)).toReal`.

result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

theorem integral_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right (hcont : ContinuousOn f (uIcc a b))
    (hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Ioi x) x)
    (hint : IntervalIntegrable f' volume a b) : ∫ y in a..b, f' y = f b - f a
declarations.doc:
Fundamental theorem of calculus-2: If `f : ℝ → E` is continuous on `[a, b]` and
  has a right derivative at `f' x` for all `x` in `[a, b)`, and `f'` is integrable on `[a, b]` then
  `∫ y in a..b, f' y` equals `f b - f a`.
declarations.type:
∀ {E : Type u_3} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup.{u_3} E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace.{0, u_3} Real E] {a b : Real}
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace.{u_3} E] {f f' : Real → E},
  ContinuousOn.{0, u_3} f (Set.uIcc.{0} a b) →
    (∀ (x : Real),
        Membership.mem.{0, 0} (Set.Ioo.{0} (Min.min.{0} a b) (Max.max.{0} a b)) x →
          HasDerivWithinAt.{0, u_3} f (f' x) (Set.Ioi.{0} x) x) →
      IntervalIntegrable.{u_3} f' MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{0} a b →
        Eq.{u_3 + 1} (∫ (y : Real) in a..b, f' y) (HSub.hSub.{u_3, u_3, u_3} (f b) (f a))

the right derivative of the function as a CDF.
For nonconvex functions it is defined as the zero measure.
declarations.type: (Real → Real) → MeasureTheory.Measure.{0} Real

declarations.name: ConvexOn.convex_taylor
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem convex_taylor (hf : ConvexOn ℝ univ f) (hf_cont : Continuous f) {a b : ℝ} :
    f b - f a - (rightDeriv f a) * (b - a)  = ∫ x in a..b, b - x ∂(curvatureMeasure f)
declarations.doc:
A Taylor formula for convex functions in terms of the right derivative
and the curvature measure.
declarations.type:
∀ {f : Real → Real},
  ConvexOn.{0, 0, 0} Real Set.univ.{0} f →
    Continuous.{0, 0} f →
      ∀ {a b : Real},
        Eq.{1}
          (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (f b) (f a))
            (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f a) (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} b a)))
          (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} b x ∂ConvexOn.curvatureMeasure f)
declarations.conclusion:
Eq.{1}
  (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (f b) (f a))
    (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f a) (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} b a)))
  (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} b x ∂ConvexOn.curvatureMeasure f)

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_integrable
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_integrable
    (hu : ∀ x, HasDerivAt u (u' x) x) (hv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt v (v' x) x)
    (huv' : Integrable (u * v')) (hu'v : Integrable (u' * v)) (huv : Integrable (u * v)) :
    ∫ (x : ℝ), u x * v' x = - ∫ (x : ℝ), u' x * v x
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts on (-∞, ∞).**
Version assuming that the total function is integrable

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.integral_bilinear_hasDerivAt_right_eq_sub
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_bilinear_hasDerivAt_right_eq_sub [CompleteSpace G]
    (hu : ∀ x, HasDerivAt u (u' x) x) (hv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt v (v' x) x)
    (huv' : Integrable (fun x ↦ L (u x) (v' x))) (hu'v : Integrable (fun x ↦ L (u' x) (v x)))
    (h_bot : Tendsto (fun x ↦ L (u x) (v x)) atBot (𝓝 m))
    (h_top : Tendsto (fun x ↦ L (u x) (v x)) atTop (𝓝 n)) :
    ∫ (x : ℝ), L (u x) (v' x) = n - m - ∫ (x : ℝ), L (u' x) (v x)
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts on (-∞, ∞).**
With respect to a general bilinear form. For the specific case of multiplication, see
`integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_hasDeriv_right
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_hasDeriv_right {u v u' v' : ℝ → A}
    (hu : ContinuousOn u [[a, b]])
    (hv : ContinuousOn v [[a, b]])
    (huu' : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivWithinAt u (u' x) (Ioi x) x)
    (hvv' : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivWithinAt v (v' x) (Ioi x) x)
    (hu' : IntervalIntegrable u' volume a b)
    (hv' : IntervalIntegrable v' volume a b) :
    ∫ x in a..b, u x * v' x = u b * v b - u a * v a - ∫ x in a..b, u' x * v x
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts**. For improper integrals, see
`MeasureTheory.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`,
`MeasureTheory.integral_Ioi_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`,
and `MeasureTheory.integral_Iic_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`.

    (hv : ∀ x ∈ [[a, b]], HasDerivWithinAt v (v' x) [[a, b]] x)
    (hu' : IntervalIntegrable u' volume a b)
    (hv' : IntervalIntegrable v' volume a b) :
    ∫ x in a..b, u x * v' x = u b * v b - u a * v a - ∫ x in a..b, u' x * v x
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts**. Special case of
`intervalIntegrable.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_hasDeriv_right`
where the functions have a one-sided derivative at the endpoints.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul [CompleteSpace A]
    (hu : ∀ x, HasDerivAt u (u' x) x) (hv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt v (v' x) x)
    (huv' : Integrable (u * v')) (hu'v : Integrable (u' * v))

For finite intervals, see: `intervalIntegral.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`.

    (π : Measure Θ) [IsFiniteMeasure π] [IsSFiniteKernel κ] :
    bayesianRisk E P κ π = ∫⁻ x, ∫⁻ z, ∫⁻ θ, E.ℓ (E.y θ, z) ∂(P†π) x ∂κ x ∂(P ∘ₘ π)
declarations.type:
∀ {Θ : Type u_1} {𝒳 : Type u_3} {𝒴 : Type u_6} {𝒵 : Type u_7} {mΘ : MeasurableSpace.{u_1} Θ}
  {m𝒳 : MeasurableSpace.{u_3} 𝒳} {m𝒴 : MeasurableSpace.{u_6} 𝒴} {m𝒵 : MeasurableSpace.{u_7} 𝒵}
  [inst : StandardBorelSpace.{u_1} Θ] [inst_1 : Nonempty.{u_1 + 1} Θ]

  [inst_2 : ProbabilityTheory.IsFiniteKernel.{u_1, u_3} P] (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.{u_3, u_7} 𝒳 𝒵)
  (π : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_1} Θ) [inst_3 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure.{u_1} π]

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt
    (f_intble : Integrable f μ) (f_nn : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f) :
    ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ = ∫ t in Set.Ioi 0, ENNReal.toReal (μ {a : α | t < f a})
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For an integrable a.e.-nonnegative real-valued function `f`, the Bochner integral of `f` can be
written (roughly speaking) as: `∫ f ∂μ = ∫ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt` for a version with Lebesgue integral `∫⁻`
instead.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.BoundedContinuousFunction.integral_eq_integral_meas_le
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma BoundedContinuousFunction.integral_eq_integral_meas_le
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α]
    (f : α →ᵇ ℝ) (μ : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (f_nn : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f) :
    ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ = ∫ t in Ioc 0 ‖f‖, ENNReal.toReal (μ {a : α | t ≤ f a})
declarations.doc:
A version of the layer cake formula for bounded continuous functions and finite measures:
∫ f dμ = ∫ t in (0, ‖f‖], μ {x | f(x) ≥ t} dt.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul_of_measurable_of_sigmaFinite
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul_of_measurable_of_sigmaFinite
    (μ : Measure α) [SFinite μ]
    (f_nn : 0 ≤ f) (f_mble : Measurable f)
    (g_intble : ∀ t > 0, IntervalIntegrable g volume 0 t) (g_mble : Measurable g)
    (g_nn : ∀ t > 0, 0 ≤ g t) :
    ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal (∫ t in (0)..f ω, g t) ∂μ =
      ∫⁻ t in Ioi 0, μ {a : α | t ≤ f a} * ENNReal.ofReal (g t)
declarations.doc:
An auxiliary version of the layer cake formula (Cavalieri's principle, tail probability
formula), with a measurability assumption that would also essentially follow from the
integrability assumptions, and a sigma-finiteness assumption.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul` and
`MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul` for the main formulations of the layer
cake formula.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le` for a version with sets of the form `{ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`
instead.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul_of_measurable
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul_of_measurable (μ : Measure α)
    (f_nn : 0 ≤ f) (f_mble : Measurable f)
    (g_intble : ∀ t > 0, IntervalIntegrable g volume 0 t) (g_mble : Measurable g)
    (g_nn : ∀ t > 0, 0 ≤ g t) :
    ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal (∫ t in (0)..f ω, g t) ∂μ =
      ∫⁻ t in Ioi 0, μ {a : α | t ≤ f a} * ENNReal.ofReal (g t)
declarations.doc:
An auxiliary version of the layer cake formula (Cavalieri's principle, tail probability
formula), with a measurability assumption that would also essentially follow from the
integrability assumptions.
Compared to `lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul_of_measurable_of_sigmaFinite`, we remove
the sigma-finite assumption.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul` and
`MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul` for the main formulations of the layer
cake formula.

declarations.name: ConvexOn.rightDerivStieltjes
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable
def rightDerivStieltjes {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ConvexOn ℝ univ f) :
    StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := rightDeriv f

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

references.statement:
For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function and $x,y \in \mathbb {R}$, \begin{align*}  f(y) - f(x) - (y - x)f’_+(x) & = \int _{z \in (x,y]} (y - z) \partial \gamma _f &  \text{ if } x \le y \:  ,
f(y) - f(x) - (y - x)f’_+(x) & = \int _{z \in (y,x]} (z - y) \partial \gamma _f &  \text{ if } y \le x \:  . \end{align*}

lemma integral_max_eq_integral_abs [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] :
    ∫ x, max 0 (γ - β * ((∂μ/∂ν) x).toReal) ∂ν
      = 2⁻¹ * (∫ x, |β * ((∂μ/∂ν) x).toReal - γ| ∂ν + γ * (ν univ).toReal - β * (μ univ).toReal
        + β * ((μ.singularPart ν) univ).toReal)

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right (hcont : ContinuousOn f (uIcc a b))
    (hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Ioi x) x)
    (hint : IntervalIntegrable f' volume a b) : ∫ y in a..b, f' y = f b - f a
declarations.doc:
Fundamental theorem of calculus-2: If `f : ℝ → E` is continuous on `[a, b]` and
  has a right derivative at `f' x` for all `x` in `[a, b)`, and `f'` is integrable on `[a, b]` then

theorem integral_deriv_mul_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right {u v u' v' : ℝ → A}
    (hu : ContinuousOn u [[a, b]])
    (hv : ContinuousOn v [[a, b]])
    (huu' : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivWithinAt u (u' x) (Ioi x) x)
    (hvv' : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivWithinAt v (v' x) (Ioi x) x)
    (hu' : IntervalIntegrable u' volume a b)
    (hv' : IntervalIntegrable v' volume a b) :
    ∫ x in a..b, u' x * v x + u x * v' x = u b * v b - u a * v a
declarations.doc:
The integral of the derivative of a product of two maps.
For improper integrals, see `MeasureTheory.integral_deriv_mul_eq_sub`,
`MeasureTheory.integral_Ioi_deriv_mul_eq_sub`, and `MeasureTheory.integral_Iic_deriv_mul_eq_sub`.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right_of_le
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem integral_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right_of_le (hab : a ≤ b) (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b))
    (hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Ioi x) x)
    (f'int : IntervalIntegrable f' volume a b) : ∫ y in a..b, f' y = f b - f a
declarations.doc:
**Fundamental theorem of calculus-2**: If `f : ℝ → E` is continuous on `[a, b]` (where `a ≤ b`)
  and has a right derivative at `f' x` for all `x` in `(a, b)`, and `f'` is integrable on `[a, b]`,
  then `∫ y in a..b, f' y` equals `f b - f a`.

declarations.doc:
Special case of `integral_deriv_mul_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right` where the functions have a
  derivative at the endpoints.

declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For an integrable a.e.-nonnegative real-valued function `f`, the Bochner integral of `f` can be
written (roughly speaking) as: `∫ f ∂μ = ∫ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt` for a version with Lebesgue integral `∫⁻`
instead.

declarations.name: Monotone.stieltjesFunction
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.Monotone.stieltjesFunction {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Monotone f) :
    StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := rightLim f
  mono' _ _ hxy := hf.rightLim hxy
  right_continuous' := by
    intro x s hs
    obtain ⟨l, u, hlu, lus⟩ : ∃ l u : ℝ, rightLim f x ∈ Ioo l u ∧ Ioo l u ⊆ s :=
      mem_nhds_iff_exists_Ioo_subset.1 hs
    obtain ⟨y, xy, h'y⟩ : ∃ (y : ℝ), x < y ∧ Ioc x y ⊆ f ⁻¹' Ioo l u :=
      mem_nhdsWithin_Ioi_iff_exists_Ioc_subset.1 (hf.tendsto_rightLim x (Ioo_mem_nhds hlu.1 hlu.2))
    change ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≥] x, rightLim f y ∈ s
    filter_upwards [Ico_mem_nhdsWithin_Ici ⟨le_refl x, xy⟩] with z hz
    apply lus
    refine ⟨hlu.1.trans_le (hf.rightLim hz.1), ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨a, za, ay⟩ : ∃ a : ℝ, z < a ∧ a < y := exists_between hz.2
    calc
      rightLim f z ≤ f a := hf.rightLim_le za
      _ < u := (h'y ⟨hz.1.trans_lt za, ay.le⟩).2
declarations.doc:
If a function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is monotone, then the function mapping `x` to the right limit of `f`
at `x` is a Stieltjes function, i.e., it is monotone and right-continuous.

declarations.name: IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure
declarations.source_snippet:
class IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure {α : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace α] [MeasurableSpace α]
  (μ : Measure α) : Prop where
  exists_measure_closedBall_le_mul'' :
    ∃ C : ℝ≥0, ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] 0, ∀ x, μ (closedBall x (2 * ε)) ≤ C * μ (closedBall x ε)
declarations.doc:
A measure `μ` is said to be a uniformly locally doubling measure if there exists a constant `C`
such that for all sufficiently small radii `ε`, and for any centre, the measure of a ball of radius
`2 * ε` is bounded by `C` times the measure of the concentric ball of radius `ε`.

Note: it is important that this definition makes a demand only for sufficiently small `ε`. For
example we want hyperbolic space to carry the instance `IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure volume` but
volumes grow exponentially in hyperbolic space. To be really explicit, consider the hyperbolic plane
of curvature -1, the area of a disc of radius `ε` is `A(ε) = 2π(cosh(ε) - 1)` so
`A(2ε)/A(ε) ~ exp(ε)`.

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae
· refine Filter.Eventually.of_forall ?_
  intro x hx
  rw [if_neg]
  · have hxu : (1 : ℝ) < x ∧ x ≤ t := by
      rcases Set.mem_uIoc.mp hx with h | h
      · exact h
      · exfalso
        nlinarith [h.1, h.2, ht]
    have h0le : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (1 : ℝ) * t - x := by nlinarith [hxu.2]
    rw [max_eq_right h0le]

  · intro hle
    have hxu : (1 : ℝ) < x ∧ x ≤ t := by
      rcases Set.mem_uIoc.mp hx with h | h
      · exact h
      · exfalso
        nlinarith [h.1, h.2, ht]
    nlinarith [hxu.1, hle]
· intro x hx
  change (1 : ℝ) < x ∧ x ≤ t
  by_cases hle : x ≤ (1 : ℝ)
  · exfalso

    apply hx
    rw [if_pos hle]
    have h : x - (1 : ℝ) * t ≤ 0 := by nlinarith [hle, ht]
    exact max_eq_left h
  · constructor
    · exact lt_of_not_ge hle
    · by_contra hxt
      change ((if x ≤ (1 : ℝ) then max (0 : ℝ) (x - (1 : ℝ) * t) else max (0 : ℝ) ((1 : ℝ) * t - x)) ≠ 0) at hx

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function and $x,y \in \mathbb {R}$, \begin{align*}  f(y) - f(x) - (y - x)f’_+(x) & = \int _{z \in (x,y]} (y - z) \partial \gamma _f &  \text{ if } x \le y \:  ,
f(y) - f(x) - (y - x)f’_+(x) & = \int _{z \in (y,x]} (z - y) \partial \gamma _f &  \text{ if } y \le x \:  . \end{align*}

library_facts.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {mα : MeasurableSpace.{u_1} α} {f g : Real → Real} (μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_1} α),
  (∀ (x : Real), GE.ge.{0} x 0 → Eq.{1} (f x) (g x)) →

library_facts.name: ProbabilityTheory.fDiv_congr_measure
library_facts.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {mα : MeasurableSpace.{u_1} α} {mβ : MeasurableSpace.{u_2} β} {f : Real → Real}
  {μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_1} α} {μ' ν' : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_2} β},
  Iff (MeasureTheory.Integrable.{0, u_1} (fun x => f (ENNReal.toReal (MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv.{u_1} μ ν x))) ν)
      (MeasureTheory.Integrable.{0, u_2} (fun x => f (ENNReal.toReal (MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv.{u_2} μ' ν' x)))
        ν') →
    (MeasureTheory.Integrable.{0, u_1} (fun x => f (ENNReal.toReal (MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv.{u_1} μ ν x))) ν →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable.{0, u_2} (fun x => f (ENNReal.toReal (MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv.{u_2} μ' ν' x)))
            ν' →
          Eq.{1} (∫ (x : α), f (ENNReal.toReal (MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv.{u_1} μ ν x)) ∂ν)
            (∫ (x : β), f (ENNReal.toReal (MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv.{u_2} μ' ν' x)) ∂ν')) →
      Eq.{1} ((MeasureTheory.Measure.singularPart.{u_1} μ ν) Set.univ.{u_1})
          ((MeasureTheory.Measure.singularPart.{u_2} μ' ν') Set.univ.{u_2}) →
        Eq.{1} (ProbabilityTheory.fDiv.{u_1} f μ ν) (ProbabilityTheory.fDiv.{u_2} f μ' ν')

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

references.name: convex_taylor
references.statement:
For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function and $x,y \in \mathbb {R}$, \begin{align*}  f(y) - f(x) - (y - x)f’_+(x) & = \int _{z \in (x,y]} (y - z) \partial \gamma _f &  \text{ if } x \le y \:  ,
f(y) - f(x) - (y - x)f’_+(x) & = \int _{z \in (y,x]} (z - y) \partial \gamma _f &  \text{ if } y \le x \:  . \end{align*}

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le` for a version with sets of the form `{ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`
instead.

lemma integral_max_eq_integral_abs [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] :
    ∫ x, max 0 (γ - β * ((∂μ/∂ν) x).toReal) ∂ν
      = 2⁻¹ * (∫ x, |β * ((∂μ/∂ν) x).toReal - γ| ∂ν + γ * (ν univ).toReal - β * (μ univ).toReal
        + β * ((μ.singularPart ν) univ).toReal)

Auxiliary lemma for `fDiv_statInfoFun_eq_integral_abs_of_nonneg_of_le` and
`fDiv_statInfoFun_eq_integral_abs_of_nonpos_of_le`.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt
    (f_intble : Integrable f μ) (f_nn : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f) :
    ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ = ∫ t in Set.Ioi 0, ENNReal.toReal (μ {a : α | t < f a})
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For an integrable a.e.-nonnegative real-valued function `f`, the Bochner integral of `f` can be
written (roughly speaking) as: `∫ f ∂μ = ∫ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt` for a version with Lebesgue integral `∫⁻`
instead.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.BoundedContinuousFunction.integral_eq_integral_meas_le
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma BoundedContinuousFunction.integral_eq_integral_meas_le
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α]
    (f : α →ᵇ ℝ) (μ : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (f_nn : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f) :
    ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ = ∫ t in Ioc 0 ‖f‖, ENNReal.toReal (μ {a : α | t ≤ f a})
declarations.doc:
A version of the layer cake formula for bounded continuous functions and finite measures:
∫ f dμ = ∫ t in (0, ‖f‖], μ {x | f(x) ≥ t} dt.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.BoundedContinuousFunction.integral_eq_integral_meas_le_of_hasFiniteIntegral
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma BoundedContinuousFunction.integral_eq_integral_meas_le_of_hasFiniteIntegral
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α]
    (f : α →ᵇ ℝ) (μ : Measure α) (f_nn : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f) (hf : HasFiniteIntegral f μ) :
    ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ = ∫ t in Ioc 0 ‖f‖, ENNReal.toReal (μ {a : α | t ≤ f a})
declarations.doc:
A version of the layer cake formula for bounded continuous functions which have finite integral:
∫ f dμ = ∫ t in (0, ‖f‖], μ {x | f(x) ≥ t} dt.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul :
    ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal (f ω ^ p) ∂μ =
      ENNReal.ofReal p * ∫⁻ t in Ioi 0, μ {a : α | t ≤ f a} * ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ (p - 1))
declarations.doc:
An application of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f^p ∂μ = p * ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, t^(p-1) * μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul` for a version with sets of the form
`{ω | f(ω) > t}` instead.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap_of_hasCompactSupport
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma integral_integral_swap_of_hasCompactSupport
    {f : X → Y → E} (hf : Continuous f.uncurry) (h'f : HasCompactSupport f.uncurry)
    {μ : Measure X} {ν : Measure Y} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ] [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν] :
    ∫ x, (∫ y, f x y ∂ν) ∂μ = ∫ y, (∫ x, f x y ∂μ) ∂ν
declarations.doc:
A version of *Fubini theorem* for continuous functions with compact support: one may swap
the order of integration with respect to locally finite measures. One does not assume that the
measures are σ-finite, contrary to the usual Fubini theorem.

theorem integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul [CompleteSpace A]
    (hu : ∀ x, HasDerivAt u (u' x) x) (hv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt v (v' x) x)
    (huv' : Integrable (u * v')) (hu'v : Integrable (u' * v))
    (h_bot : Tendsto (u * v) atBot (𝓝 a')) (h_top : Tendsto (u * v) atTop (𝓝 b')) :
    ∫ (x : ℝ), u x * v' x = b' - a' - ∫ (x : ℝ), u' x * v x
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts on (-∞, ∞).**
For finite intervals, see: `intervalIntegral.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`.

theorem convex_taylor (hf : ConvexOn ℝ univ f) (hf_cont : Continuous f) {a b : ℝ} :

and the curvature measure.

            (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f a) (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} b a)))

declarations.name: ImplicitFunctionData
declarations.source_snippet:
structure ImplicitFunctionData (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] (E : Type*)
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (F : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup F]
    [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] [CompleteSpace F] (G : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G]
    [CompleteSpace G] where
  leftFun : E → F
  leftDeriv : E →L[𝕜] F
  rightFun : E → G
  rightDeriv : E →L[𝕜] G
  pt : E
  left_has_deriv : HasStrictFDerivAt leftFun leftDeriv pt
  right_has_deriv : HasStrictFDerivAt rightFun rightDeriv pt
  left_range : range leftDeriv = ⊤
  right_range : range rightDeriv = ⊤
  isCompl_ker : IsCompl (ker leftDeriv) (ker rightDeriv)

declarations.doc:
**Fundamental theorem of calculus-1**: if `f : ℝ → E` is integrable on `a..b` and `f` is
continuous at `b`, then `u ↦ ∫ x in a..u, f x` has derivative `f b` at `b`.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.deriv_integral_of_tendsto_ae_right
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem deriv_integral_of_tendsto_ae_right (hf : IntervalIntegrable f volume a b)
    (hmeas : StronglyMeasurableAtFilter f (𝓝 b)) (hb : Tendsto f (𝓝 b ⊓ ae volume) (𝓝 c)) :
    deriv (fun u => ∫ x in a..u, f x) b = c
declarations.doc:
Fundamental theorem of calculus: if `f : ℝ → E` is integrable on `a..b` and `f` has a finite
limit `c` almost surely at `b`, then the derivative of `u ↦ ∫ x in a..u, f x` at `b` equals `c`.

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le` for a version with sets of the form `{ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`
instead.

declarations.name: Monotone.stieltjesFunction
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.Monotone.stieltjesFunction {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Monotone f) :
    StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := rightLim f
  mono' _ _ hxy := hf.rightLim hxy
  right_continuous' := by
    intro x s hs
    obtain ⟨l, u, hlu, lus⟩ : ∃ l u : ℝ, rightLim f x ∈ Ioo l u ∧ Ioo l u ⊆ s :=
      mem_nhds_iff_exists_Ioo_subset.1 hs
    obtain ⟨y, xy, h'y⟩ : ∃ (y : ℝ), x < y ∧ Ioc x y ⊆ f ⁻¹' Ioo l u :=
      mem_nhdsWithin_Ioi_iff_exists_Ioc_subset.1 (hf.tendsto_rightLim x (Ioo_mem_nhds hlu.1 hlu.2))
    change ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≥] x, rightLim f y ∈ s
    filter_upwards [Ico_mem_nhdsWithin_Ici ⟨le_refl x, xy⟩] with z hz
    apply lus
    refine ⟨hlu.1.trans_le (hf.rightLim hz.1), ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨a, za, ay⟩ : ∃ a : ℝ, z < a ∧ a < y := exists_between hz.2
    calc
      rightLim f z ≤ f a := hf.rightLim_le za
      _ < u := (h'y ⟨hz.1.trans_lt za, ay.le⟩).2
declarations.doc:
If a function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is monotone, then the function mapping `x` to the right limit of `f`
at `x` is a Stieltjes function, i.e., it is monotone and right-continuous.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral
declarations.source_snippet:
def intervalIntegral (f : ℝ → E) (a b : ℝ) (μ : Measure ℝ) : E :=
  (∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂μ) - ∫ x in Ioc b a, f x ∂μ

notation3"∫ "(...)" in "a".."b", "r:60:(scoped f => f)" ∂"μ:70 => intervalIntegral r a b μ

notation3"∫ "(...)" in "a".."b", "r:60:(scoped f => intervalIntegral f a b volume) => r
declarations.doc:
The interval integral `∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ` is defined
as `∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Ioc b a, f x ∂μ`. If `a ≤ b`, then it equals
`∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂μ`, otherwise it equals `-∫ x in Ioc b a, f x ∂μ`.

declarations.name: StieltjesFunction.length
declarations.source_snippet:
def length (s : Set ℝ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (a) (b) (_ : s ⊆ Ioc a b), ofReal (f b - f a)

declarations.name: StieltjesFunction.add
declarations.source_snippet:
protected def add (f g : StieltjesFunction) : StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := fun x => f x + g x
  mono' := f.mono.add g.mono
  right_continuous' := fun x => (f.right_continuous x).add (g.right_continuous x)
declarations.doc: The sum of two Stieltjes functions is a Stieltjes function.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.deriv_integral_right
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem deriv_integral_right (hf : IntervalIntegrable f volume a b)
    (hmeas : StronglyMeasurableAtFilter f (𝓝 b)) (hb : ContinuousAt f b) :
    deriv (fun u => ∫ x in a..u, f x) b = f b
declarations.doc:
Fundamental theorem of calculus: if `f : ℝ → E` is integrable on `a..b` and `f` is continuous
at `b`, then the derivative of `u ↦ ∫ x in a..u, f x` at `b` equals `f b`.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.deriv_integral_left
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem deriv_integral_left (hf : IntervalIntegrable f volume a b)
    (hmeas : StronglyMeasurableAtFilter f (𝓝 a)) (hb : ContinuousAt f a) :
    deriv (fun u => ∫ x in u..b, f x) a = -f a
declarations.doc:
Fundamental theorem of calculus: if `f : ℝ → E` is integrable on `a..b` and `f` is continuous
at `a`, then the derivative of `u ↦ ∫ x in u..b, f x` at `a` equals `-f a`.

declarations.name: integral_stieltjes_meas_by_parts
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma integral_stieltjes_meas_by_parts (f g : StieltjesFunction) (a b : ℝ)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) :
    ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂g.measure = (f b) * (g b) - (f a) * (g a) - ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂f.measure
declarations.type:
∀ (f g : StieltjesFunction) (a b : Real),
  ContinuousOn.{0, 0} (↑f) (Set.Icc.{0} a b) →
    Eq.{1} (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, ↑f x ∂StieltjesFunction.measure g)
      (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f b) (↑g b)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f a) (↑g a)))
        (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, ↑g x ∂StieltjesFunction.measure f))
declarations.conclusion:
Eq.{1} (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, ↑f x ∂StieltjesFunction.measure g)
  (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f b) (↑g b)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (↑f a) (↑g a)))
    (∫ (x : Real) in a..b, ↑g x ∂StieltjesFunction.measure f))

      = 2⁻¹ * (∫ x, |β * ((∂μ/∂ν) x).toReal - γ| ∂ν + γ * (ν univ).toReal - β * (μ univ).toReal
        + β * ((μ.singularPart ν) univ).toReal)

theorem integral_smul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_smul_of_integrable
    {f : E → 𝕜} {g : E → G} {v : E}
    (hf'g : Integrable (fun x ↦ fderiv ℝ f x v • g x) μ)
    (hfg' : Integrable (fun x ↦ f x • fderiv ℝ g x v) μ)
    (hfg : Integrable (fun x ↦ f x • g x) μ)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (hg : Differentiable ℝ g) :
    ∫ x, f x • fderiv ℝ g x v ∂μ = - ∫ x, fderiv ℝ f x v • g x ∂μ

**Integration by parts for Fréchet derivatives**
Version with a scalar function: `∫ f • g' = - ∫ f' • g` when `f • g'` and `f' • g` and `f • g`
are integrable, where `f'` and `g'` are the derivatives of `f` and `g` in a given direction `v`.

theorem integral_bilinear_fderiv_right_eq_neg_left_of_integrable
    {f : E → F} {g : E → G} {v : E} {B : F →L[ℝ] G →L[ℝ] W}
    (hf'g : Integrable (fun x ↦ B (fderiv ℝ f x v) (g x)) μ)
    (hfg' : Integrable (fun x ↦ B (f x) (fderiv ℝ g x v)) μ)
    (hfg : Integrable (fun x ↦ B (f x) (g x)) μ)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (hg : Differentiable ℝ g) :
    ∫ x, B (f x) (fderiv ℝ g x v) ∂μ = - ∫ x, B (fderiv ℝ f x v) (g x) ∂μ
declarations.doc:
**Integration by parts for Fréchet derivatives**
Version with a general bilinear form `B`.
If `B f g` is integrable, as well as `B f' g` and `B f g'` where `f'` and `g'` are the derivatives
of `f` and `g` in a given direction `v`, then `∫ B f g' = - ∫ B f' g`.

declarations.source_snippet:
theorem sum_range_by_parts :
    ∑ i ∈ range n, f i • g i =
      f (n - 1) • G n - ∑ i ∈ range (n - 1), (f (i + 1) - f i) • G (i + 1)
declarations.doc: **Summation by parts** for ranges

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt` for a version with sets of the form
`{ω | f(ω) > t}` instead.

lemma integral_max_eq_integral_abs [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] :
    ∫ x, max 0 (γ - β * ((∂μ/∂ν) x).toReal) ∂ν
      = 2⁻¹ * (∫ x, |β * ((∂μ/∂ν) x).toReal - γ| ∂ν + γ * (ν univ).toReal - β * (μ univ).toReal
        + β * ((μ.singularPart ν) univ).toReal)

theorem lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul_of_measurable (μ : Measure α)
    (f_nn : 0 ≤ f) (f_mble : Measurable f)
    (g_intble : ∀ t > 0, IntervalIntegrable g volume 0 t) (g_mble : Measurable g)
    (g_nn : ∀ t > 0, 0 ≤ g t) :
    ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal (∫ t in (0)..f ω, g t) ∂μ =
      ∫⁻ t in Ioi 0, μ {a : α | t ≤ f a} * ENNReal.ofReal (g t)
declarations.doc:
An auxiliary version of the layer cake formula (Cavalieri's principle, tail probability
formula), with a measurability assumption that would also essentially follow from the
integrability assumptions.
Compared to `lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul_of_measurable_of_sigmaFinite`, we remove
the sigma-finite assumption.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul` and
`MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul` for the main formulations of the layer
cake formula.

An auxiliary version of the layer cake formula (Cavalieri's principle, tail probability
formula), with a measurability assumption that would also essentially follow from the
integrability assumptions, and a sigma-finiteness assumption.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul` and
`MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul` for the main formulations of the layer
cake formula.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le` for a version with sets of the form `{ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`
instead.

theorem lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_le_mul :
    ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal (f ω ^ p) ∂μ =
      ENNReal.ofReal p * ∫⁻ t in Ioi 0, μ {a : α | t ≤ f a} * ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ (p - 1))
declarations.doc:
An application of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f^p ∂μ = p * ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, t^(p-1) * μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul` for a version with sets of the form
`{ω | f(ω) > t}` instead.

theorem integral_indicator (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    ∫ x, indicator s f x ∂μ = ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ
declarations.doc:

over the whole space is equal to `∫ x in s, f x ∂μ` defined as `∫ x, f x ∂(μ.restrict s)`.

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

references.name: convex_taylor
references.statement:
For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function and $x,y \in \mathbb {R}$, \begin{align*}  f(y) - f(x) - (y - x)f’_+(x) & = \int _{z \in (x,y]} (y - z) \partial \gamma _f &  \text{ if } x \le y \:  ,
f(y) - f(x) - (y - x)f’_+(x) & = \int _{z \in (y,x]} (z - y) \partial \gamma _f &  \text{ if } y \le x \:  . \end{align*}

instead.

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt` for a version with sets of the form
`{ω | f(ω) > t}` instead.

declarations.name: Monotone.stieltjesFunction
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def _root_.Monotone.stieltjesFunction {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Monotone f) :
    StieltjesFunction where
  toFun := rightLim f
  mono' _ _ hxy := hf.rightLim hxy
  right_continuous' := by
    intro x s hs
    obtain ⟨l, u, hlu, lus⟩ : ∃ l u : ℝ, rightLim f x ∈ Ioo l u ∧ Ioo l u ⊆ s :=
      mem_nhds_iff_exists_Ioo_subset.1 hs
    obtain ⟨y, xy, h'y⟩ : ∃ (y : ℝ), x < y ∧ Ioc x y ⊆ f ⁻¹' Ioo l u :=
      mem_nhdsWithin_Ioi_iff_exists_Ioc_subset.1 (hf.tendsto_rightLim x (Ioo_mem_nhds hlu.1 hlu.2))
    change ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≥] x, rightLim f y ∈ s
    filter_upwards [Ico_mem_nhdsWithin_Ici ⟨le_refl x, xy⟩] with z hz
    apply lus
    refine ⟨hlu.1.trans_le (hf.rightLim hz.1), ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨a, za, ay⟩ : ∃ a : ℝ, z < a ∧ a < y := exists_between hz.2
    calc
      rightLim f z ≤ f a := hf.rightLim_le za
      _ < u := (h'y ⟨hz.1.trans_lt za, ay.le⟩).2
declarations.doc:
If a function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is monotone, then the function mapping `x` to the right limit of `f`
at `x` is a Stieltjes function, i.e., it is monotone and right-continuous.

    = ⨅ z, ∫⁻ θ, E.ℓ (E.y θ, z) ∂(P†π) x

/-- Given a Generalized Bayes estimator `f`, we can define a deterministic kernel. -/
declarations.doc:
We say that a measurable function `f : 𝒳 → 𝒵` is a Generalized Bayes estimator for the
estimation problem `E` with respect to the prior `π` if for `(P ∘ₘ π)`-almost every `x` it is of
the form `x ↦ argmin_z P†π(x)[θ ↦ ℓ(y(θ), z)]`.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul
declarations.doc:
This is Exercise 1.2.1 from [tao2010]. It allows you to express integration of a measurable
function with respect to `(μ.withDensity f)` as an integral with respect to `μ`, called the base
measure. `μ` is often the Lebesgue measure, and in this circumstance `f` is the probability density
function, and `(μ.withDensity f)` represents any continuous random variable as a
probability measure, such as the uniform distribution between 0 and 1, the Gaussian distribution,
the exponential distribution, the Beta distribution, or the Cauchy distribution (see Section 2.4
of [wasserman2004]). Thus, this method shows how to one can calculate expectations, variances,
and other moments as a function of the probability density function.

The Lebesgue integral of `g` with respect to the measure `μ.withDensity f` coincides with

version without conditions on `g` but requiring that `f` is almost everywhere finite, see
`lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul_non_measurable`

declarations.name: VectorFourier.fourierPowSMulRight_iteratedFDeriv_fourierIntegral
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem fourierPowSMulRight_iteratedFDeriv_fourierIntegral [FiniteDimensional ℝ V]
    {μ : Measure V} [Measure.IsAddHaarMeasure μ] {K N : ℕ∞} (hf : ContDiff ℝ N f)
    (h'f : ∀ (k n : ℕ), k ≤ K → n ≤ N → Integrable (fun v ↦ ‖v‖^k * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n f v‖) μ)
    {k n : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ K) (hn : n ≤ N) {w : W} :
    fourierPowSMulRight (-L.flip)
      (iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fourierIntegral 𝐞 μ L.toLinearMap₂ f)) w n =
    fourierIntegral 𝐞 μ L.toLinearMap₂
      (iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun v ↦ fourierPowSMulRight L f v k)) w
declarations.doc:
The `k`-th derivative of the Fourier integral of `f`, multiplied by `(L v w) ^ n`, is the
Fourier integral of the `n`-th derivative of `(L v w) ^ k * f`.

declarations.name: Continuous.deriv_integral
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem _root_.Continuous.deriv_integral (f : ℝ → E) (hf : Continuous f) (a b : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun u => ∫ x : ℝ in a..u, f x) b = f b
declarations.doc:
**Fundamental theorem of calculus-1**, derivative in the right endpoint.

If `f : ℝ → E` is continuous, then the derivative of `u ↦ ∫ x in a..u, f x` at `b` is `f b`.

declarations.name: VectorFourier.fourierIntegral_iteratedFDeriv
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem fourierIntegral_iteratedFDeriv [FiniteDimensional ℝ V]
    {μ : Measure V} [Measure.IsAddHaarMeasure μ] {N : ℕ∞} (hf : ContDiff ℝ N f)
    (h'f : ∀ (n : ℕ), n ≤ N → Integrable (iteratedFDeriv ℝ n f) μ) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ N) :
    fourierIntegral 𝐞 μ L.toLinearMap₂ (iteratedFDeriv ℝ n f)
      = (fun w ↦ fourierPowSMulRight (-L.flip) (fourierIntegral 𝐞 μ L.toLinearMap₂ f) w n)
declarations.doc:
The Fourier integral of the `n`-th derivative of a function is obtained by multiplying the
Fourier integral of the original function by `(2πI L w ⬝ )^n`.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.measure_integral_sub_integral_sub_linear_isLittleO_of_tendsto_ae_right
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem measure_integral_sub_integral_sub_linear_isLittleO_of_tendsto_ae_right
    (hab : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) (hmeas : StronglyMeasurableAtFilter f lb' μ)
    (hf : Tendsto f (lb' ⊓ ae μ) (𝓝 c)) (hu : Tendsto u lt lb) (hv : Tendsto v lt lb) :
    (fun t => ((∫ x in a..v t, f x ∂μ) - ∫ x in a..u t, f x ∂μ) - ∫ _ in u t..v t, c ∂μ) =o[lt]
      fun t => ∫ _ in u t..v t, (1 : ℝ) ∂μ
declarations.doc:
**Fundamental theorem of calculus-1**, strict derivative in right endpoint for a locally finite
measure.

Let `f` be a measurable function integrable on `a..b`. Let `(lb, lb')` be a pair of
`intervalIntegral.FTCFilter`s around `b`. Suppose that `f` has a finite limit `c` at `lb' ⊓ ae μ`.

Then `∫ x in a..v, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in a..u, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in u..v, c ∂μ + o(∫ x in u..v, (1:ℝ) ∂μ)` as
`u` and `v` tend to `lb`.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral.deriv_integral_right

theorem deriv_integral_right (hf : IntervalIntegrable f volume a b)
    (hmeas : StronglyMeasurableAtFilter f (𝓝 b)) (hb : ContinuousAt f b) :
    deriv (fun u => ∫ x in a..u, f x) b = f b
declarations.doc:
Fundamental theorem of calculus: if `f : ℝ → E` is integrable on `a..b` and `f` is continuous
at `b`, then the derivative of `u ↦ ∫ x in a..u, f x` at `b` equals `f b`.

result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

noncomputable
def rightDerivStieltjes {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ConvexOn ℝ univ f) :
    StieltjesFunction where

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le` for a version with sets of the form `{ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`
instead.

declarations.name: Convex.taylor_approx_two_segment
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem Convex.taylor_approx_two_segment {v w : E} (hv : x + v ∈ interior s)
    (hw : x + v + w ∈ interior s) :
    (fun h : ℝ => f (x + h • v + h • w)
        - f (x + h • v) - h • f' x w - h ^ 2 • f'' v w - (h ^ 2 / 2) • f'' w w) =o[𝓝[>] 0]
      fun h => h ^ 2
declarations.doc:
Assume that `f` is differentiable inside a convex set `s`, and that its derivative `f'` is
differentiable at a point `x`. Then, given two vectors `v` and `w` pointing inside `s`, one can
Taylor-expand to order two the function `f` on the segment `[x + h v, x + h (v + w)]`, giving a
bilinear estimate for `f (x + hv + hw) - f (x + hv)` in terms of `f' w` and of `f'' ⬝ w`, up to
`o(h^2)`.

This is a technical statement used to show that the second derivative is symmetric.

declarations.source_snippet:
theorem lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq (μ : Measure α) {p q : ℝ} (hpq : p.IsConjExponent q)
    {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) (hg : AEMeasurable g μ) :
    (∫⁻ a, (f * g) a ∂μ) ≤ (∫⁻ a, f a ^ p ∂μ) ^ (1 / p) * (∫⁻ a, g a ^ q ∂μ) ^ (1 / q)
declarations.doc:
Hölder's inequality for functions `α → ℝ≥0∞`. The integral of the product of two functions
is bounded by the product of their `ℒp` and `ℒq` seminorms when `p` and `q` are conjugate
exponents.

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

formula), with a measurability assumption that would also essentially follow from the
integrability assumptions, and a sigma-finiteness assumption.

`MeasureTheory.lintegral_comp_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul` for the main formulations of the layer
cake formula.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) > t}`.

See `lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le` for a version with sets of the form `{ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`
instead.

result.statement: For $f: \mathbb {R} \to \mathbb {R}$ a convex function, for all $x \in \mathbb {R}$~ , \begin{align*}  f(x) & = f(1) + f’_+(1) (x - 1) + \int _{y} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*}
result.proof:
By Lemma~ \ref{lem:convex_taylor}, for $x > 1$, \begin{align*}  f(x) - f(1) - f’_+(1) (x - 1) & = \int _{y \in (1, x]} (x - y) \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \max \{ 0, x - y\}  \partial \gamma _f
& = \int _{y \in (1, +\infty )} \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f \:  . \end{align*} That final integral is equal to $\int _y \phi _{1,y}(x) \partial \gamma _f$ (without the restriction to $(1, +\infty )$) because $\phi _{1,y}(x)$ is zero outside of $(1, +\infty )$ for $x \ge 1$. The case of $x < 1$ is similar.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le
declarations.doc:
The standard case of the layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula:

For a nonnegative function `f` on a measure space, the Lebesgue integral of `f` can
be written (roughly speaking) as: `∫⁻ f ∂μ = ∫⁻ t in 0..∞, μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t}`.

See `MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt` for a version with sets of the form
`{ω | f(ω) > t}` instead.
declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace.{u_1} α] {f : α → Real} (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_1} α),
  Filter.EventuallyLE.{u_1, 0} (MeasureTheory.ae.{u_1, u_1} μ) 0 f →
    AEMeasurable.{u_1, 0} f μ →
      Eq.{1} (∫⁻ (ω : α), ENNReal.ofReal (f ω) ∂μ)
        (∫⁻ (t : Real) in Set.Ioi.{0} 0, μ (setOf.{u_1} fun a => LE.le.{0} t (f a)))
declarations.conclusion:
Eq.{1} (∫⁻ (ω : α), ENNReal.ofReal (f ω) ∂μ)
  (∫⁻ (t : Real) in Set.Ioi.{0} 0, μ (setOf.{u_1} fun a => LE.le.{0} t (f a)))

        (∀ᵐ (t : Real) ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.restrict.{0} MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{0} (Set.Ioi.{0} 0),
            LE.le.{0} 0 (g t)) →
          Eq.{1} (∫⁻ (ω : α), ENNReal.ofReal (∫ (t : Real) in 0 ..f ω, g t) ∂μ)
            (∫⁻ (t : Real) in Set.Ioi.{0} 0,
              HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (μ (setOf.{u_1} fun a => LE.le.{0} t (f a))) (ENNReal.ofReal (g t)))
